hook.speaker: Bharat
hook.setting: After fourteen years, Hanuman brings Bharat the news that Ram is coming; Bharat has one question.
hook.sanskrit: तब हनुमंत नाइ पद माथा। कहे सकल रघुपति गुन गाथा॥ कहु कपि कबहुँ कृपाल गोसाईं। सुमिरहिं मोहि दास की नाईं ॥
hook.line: Tell me: does he ever think of me?
hook.translation: Then Hanuman bowed at his feet and told all of Raghupati's virtues. 'Tell me, Hanuman: does the kind master ever remember me, as one remembers a servant?'
hook.for_you: Your mind stays heavy with old pain while you try to learn.
hook.first_line: Your mind stays heavy with old pain while you try to learn.

alternates.speaker: Bhartrihari
alternates.setting: From the section on wealth: how the world treats someone who has lost money.
alternates.sanskrit: तानीन्द्रियाण्यविकलानि तदेव नाम सा बुद्धिरप्रतिहता वचनं तदेव । अर्थोष्मणा विरहितः पुरुषः क्षणेन सोऽप्यन्य एव भवतीति विचित्रमेतत् ॥
alternates.line: Same person, same mind, same voice. Lose money, and people suddenly treat you as someone else.
alternates.translation: The same faculties, unimpaired; the same name; the same unclouded mind; the same speech. Yet a man deprived of the warmth of wealth becomes, in a moment, someone else. How strange!
alternates.why: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.
alternates.misuse: The verse mocks how the world sees you; it does not measure your worth.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On wealth
prasang.summary: A wry look at money: how the world flatters the rich and forgets the broke, wealth's three destinies, and how distance and neglect ruin what we value. It closes with advice to the chataka bird not to plead before every cloud.
prasang.lesson: Money changes how others see you, not who you are. Give it, enjoy it, or lose it.

alternates.speaker: Sutikshna
alternates.setting: The young sage Sutikshna hears Ram is coming and runs to meet him, full of doubt about himself.
alternates.sanskrit: सहित अनुज मोहि राम गोसाईं। मिलिहहिं निज सेवक की नाईं॥ मोरे जियँ भरोस दृढ़ नाहीं। भगति बिरति न ग्यान मन माहीं ॥ नहिं सतसंग जोग जप जागा। नहिं दृढ़ चरन कमल अनुरागा॥ एक बानि करुनानिधान की। सो प्रिय जाकें गति न आन की ॥
alternates.line: I have no devotion, no wisdom, no steady love. But he loves the one who has nowhere else to go.
alternates.translation: 'Will Ram, my master, with his brother, meet me as he would his own servant? There is no firm trust in my heart; no devotion, detachment or wisdom in my mind; no good company, no yoga, chanting or sacrifice, no steady love for his lotus feet. But the ocean of compassion has one habit: the one who has no other refuge is dear to him.'
alternates.why: You don't have to feel qualified; the one with nowhere else to go is the one he loves.
alternates.misuse: Grace doesn't erase responsibility or consequences; it means you don't carry them alone.

prasang.title: Sutikshna runs to meet Ram
prasang.summary: A young sage hears Ram is near and runs out, sure he has no devotion, wisdom or discipline worth anything, trusting only that Ram loves those with nowhere else to go. Lost in love he wanders, dances, forgets the way; Ram watches from behind a tree, then lifts him up and holds him. Asked for a boon, the sage says only: may this one pride never leave me, that I am his.
prasang.story_hook: A young sage ran out of his hut to meet Ram and, halfway there, forgot which way he was going.
prasang.lesson: You don't have to feel qualified; the one with nowhere else to go is the one he loves.

verse.setting: After fourteen years, Hanuman brings Bharat the news that Ram is coming; Bharat has one question.
verse.sanskrit: तब हनुमंत नाइ पद माथा। कहे सकल रघुपति गुन गाथा॥ कहु कपि कबहुँ कृपाल गोसाईं। सुमिरहिं मोहि दास की नाईं ॥
verse.line: Tell me: does he ever think of me?

why: he hopes to be remembered only as a servant
fourteen years come down to one question

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.setting: Rama tells the sages how craving rules people.
verse.sanskrit: लोकोऽयमखिलं दुःखं चिन्तयोज्झितयोज्झति । तृष्णाविषूचिकामन्त्रश्चिन्तात्यागो हि कथ्यते ॥
verse.line: Let go of worry and most sorrow goes with it. That is the cure for craving.
verse.translation: People let go of all their sorrow when they let go of worry. Giving up worry is called the cure for the sickness of craving.
verse.why: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.

prasang.title: Rama's lament: what is the point of all this?
prasang.summary: Asked to speak, Rama pours out what he has seen: wealth hardens people, life drips away like water off a leaf, ego and craving run us, the mind never fills, childhood, youth and old age each bring their own suffering, and time eats everything. He ends by saying only the company of good people gives him hope.
prasang.story_hook: In front of the whole court, the young prince stood up and said what everyone feels and nobody says.
prasang.lesson: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.

why: Craving on a rope (Yoga Vasishtha 1.17)
plan_v3.writer_note: Letting-go teaching for a reader who is young and afraid of being left. Explain it through their own situation and feeling: what is released is the grip that hurts them, never their love, their hope or their work. Never say or imply 'stop caring' or 'your hope is the problem'. Read it after the guard verse, which reassures first.

guard.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
guard.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: The creation story: last of all, dharma is made.
verse.sanskrit: स नैव व्यभवत् तच्छ्रेयो रूपमत्यसृजत धर्मम् । तदेतत्क्षत्रस्य क्षत्रं यद्धर्मस्तस्माद्धर्मात् परं नास्त्यथो अबलीयान् बलीयाꣳसमाशꣳसते धर्मेण यथा राज्ञैवम् । यो वै स धर्मः सत्यं वै तत् तस्मात्सत्यं वदन्तमाहुर्धर्मं वदतीति धर्मं वा वदन्तꣳ सत्यं वदतीत्येतद्ध्येवैतदुभयं भवति ॥
verse.line: Nothing is higher than what is right. With it the weak can face the strong. What is right is truth.
verse.translation: Still he did not flourish. So he created a higher form, dharma. Dharma is the power over power; nothing is higher than dharma. Through dharma even a weak man can stand up to a strong one, as with the help of a king. That dharma is truth. So people say of one who speaks truth, 'He speaks dharma,' and of one who speaks dharma, 'He speaks truth.' Both are the same.
verse.why: Fear and loneliness are human; truth gives even the weak a footing.

prasang.title: The first being: fear, loneliness and dharma
prasang.summary: In this creation story the first being, alone, feels fear, then realises there is no one else to fear. He feels no joy alone and longs for a companion, splitting into husband and wife. Finally dharma is created, the truth by which even the weak can stand up to the strong.
prasang.lesson: Fear and loneliness are human; truth gives even the weak a footing.

why: the weaker party is not without standing
With what is right the weak can face the strong.

verse.speaker: Bhishma
verse.setting: Bhishma on public slander, answering Yudhishthira's question about being insulted in an assembly.
verse.sanskrit: परिवादं ब्रुवाणो हि दुरात्मा वै महाजने / प्रकाशयति दोषान्स्वान्सर्पः फणमिवोन्नतम्
verse.line: Whoever runs others down in public only puts their own faults on display.
verse.translation: The person who speaks ill of others in front of a crowd only puts his own faults on display, the way a snake raises its hood.
verse.why: Careless critics show their own faults. Let their words pass like a crow's cawing.

prasang.title: Bhishma on bearing slander
prasang.summary: Yudhishthira asks how to respond when a harsh fool abuses you in public. Bhishma: let it pass like a crow cawing; the slanderer only displays his own faults.
prasang.lesson: Careless critics show their own faults. Let their words pass like a crow's cawing.

why: The slandered person is not the one exposed
The public insult is turned back on the one who made it

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram to Sugriva on the marks of a good friend.
verse.sanskrit: देत लेत मन संक न धरई। बल अनुमान सदा हित करई॥ बिपति काल कर सतगुन नेहा। श्रुति कह संत मित्र गुन एहा ॥
verse.line: A good friend gives without keeping score, and loves you a hundredfold more in hard times.
verse.translation: He gives and takes without suspicion, always does you good as far as he is able, and in hard times loves you a hundred times more. These, say the scriptures, are the qualities of a good friend.
verse.why: A friend treats your trouble as bigger than their own.

prasang.title: Ram and Sugriva become friends
prasang.summary: Hanuman, sent to check whether the two strangers are Bali's spies, recognises Ram and brings him to Sugriva, who has been driven out by his brother. Before a fire as witness they become friends, and Ram describes what friendship asks: your friend's small trouble is a mountain, your own is dust; steer him right, hide his faults, love him more in hard times.
prasang.lesson: A friend treats your trouble as bigger than their own.

why: giving and taking without misgiving
love that multiplies in the friend's bad time

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: उद्यम्य धुरमुत्कर्षेदाजानेयकृतं स्मरन् / कुरु सत्वं च मानं च विद्धि पौरुषमात्मनः
verse.line: Pick up the load again. Summon your strength and self-respect, and know the power in you.
verse.translation: Lift the load and pull it forward, remembering how a thoroughbred works. Summon your strength and your self-respect; know the power that is in you.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

why: Mana, self-respect, is to be summoned

story.title: The last day of waiting
story.story_hook: There was one day left, and Bharat had begun to wonder whether he had been forgotten.
story.summary: One day is left of the fourteen years and there is no word. Bharat wonders whether Ram has forgotten him, and his mind starts to sink. Just then Hanuman arrives like a boat and says Ram is coming. Bharat says no gift could repay this news.
story.lesson: Waiting is hardest on the last day; hope can arrive just as you go under.
story.hook_title: One day was left, and Bharat began to wonder if Ram had forgotten him
story.teaser: One day was left, and Bharat began to wonder if Ram had forgotten him

verse.speaker: Tulsidas
verse.setting: Bharat walks toward Ram, slowed by shame, quickened by love.
verse.sanskrit: फेरति मनहुँ मातु कृत खोरी। चलत भगति बल धीरज धोरी॥ जब समुझत रघुनाथ सुभाऊ। तब पथ परत उताइल पाऊ ॥
verse.line: Shame slowed him. But whenever he remembered Ram's nature, his feet moved faster.
verse.translation: It was as if his mother's wrong held him back, while the strength of devotion drove him on like a patient ox. Whenever he remembered Raghunath's nature, his feet moved faster on the path.

why: his feet are pulled back by a wrong that was not his
Everyone must think I wanted this. I can't look at anyone. Will he even see me?

verse.speaker: Hanuman
verse.setting: After setting Lanka ablaze in fury, Hanuman fears he has harmed Sita and turns on his own anger.
verse.sanskrit: धन्याः खलु महात्मानो ये बुद्ध्या कोपमुत्थितम्। निरुन्धन्ति महात्मानो दीप्तमग्निमिवाम्भसा॥
verse.line: Blessed are those who use good sense to put out rising anger, the way water puts out fire.
verse.translation: Blessed indeed are the great-hearted who, with good sense, check anger the moment it rises, as water puts out a blazing fire.

words.en: like a blazing fire with water

verse.why: Anger can win a small fight and ruin the real goal.

prasang.title: Hanuman's anger and the burning of Lanka
prasang.summary: Hanuman decides to test the enemy, smashes a grove, is captured and has his tail set on fire. He burns the city in fury, then is horrified that Sita might have died in the fire: in anger, he says, he nearly wrecked the very thing he came to do.
prasang.story_hook: The city was burning behind him, and then a terrible thought stopped him cold.
prasang.lesson: Anger can win a small fight and ruin the real goal.

why: What anger made me do (Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda 55)

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verse.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
verse.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

why: Do not push yourself down; never hold yourself in contempt.
Self-reproach is shown to block every good

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.line: The remedy for weakness is not brooding over weakness, but thinking of strength.
verse.translation: But, says the Vedanta, being reminded of weakness does not help much; give strength, and strength does not come by thinking of weakness all the time. The remedy for weakness is not brooding over weakness, but thinking of strength.
verse.why: Stop rehearsing your weakness; think of your strength and act.

prasang.title: Practical Vedanta 1: faith in yourself (London, 1896)
prasang.summary: Vedanta must work in ordinary life. Calm minds do the most work, angry ones break themselves. The new religion calls the person who does not believe in himself the atheist, and the remedy for weakness is to think of strength, not brood over weakness.
prasang.lesson: Stop rehearsing your weakness; think of your strength and act.

why: going over one's faults again is declared no cure
Think of strength, not of weakness.

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.setting: 'The Common Bases of Hinduism', Lahore, November 1897.
verse.line: Learn everything that is good from others, but bring it in, and in your own way absorb it; do not become others.
verse.translation: Learn everything that is good from others, but bring it in, and in your own way absorb it; do not become others.
verse.why: Absorb the best of where you live, and grow into yourself.

prasang.title: Learn from all, imitate none (Lahore, 1897)
prasang.summary: Speaking to rival reform and orthodox groups, he looks for common ground. Religion must be realised, not repeated like a parrot. Learn everything good from others, as a seed takes in earth, air and water, but grow into your own tree and do not become others.
prasang.lesson: Absorb the best of where you live, and grow into yourself.

why: stay yourself while learning

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verse.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verse.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: A person must lift themselves up by their own effort and must not let themselves sink. The self is the only friend, and the self is the only enemy. No outside force can do this for you.
verse.try_today: Name one thing you can do today to lift your own weight.

why: self-respect: you are the one who can lift you
Lift yourself by yourself

story.title: Vairagyashatakam: Censure of begging and servility
story.summary: On the humiliation of begging favours from the rich: only hungry children could make a proud man ask. Contentment, not wealth, is real joy.
story.lesson: Keep your dignity; ask for help for others before you ever grovel for yourself.
story.teaser: Vairagyashatakam: Censure of begging and servility

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks what drives people to do wrong against their will; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचअथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः । अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥
verse.line: Why do I do the wrong thing even when I don't want to, as if something forces me?
verse.translation: Arjuna said: Then what drives a person to do wrong, Krishna, even against his will, as if pushed by force?

words.en: O descendant of the Vrishni clan

verse.why: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.

prasang.title: Restraining desire
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks why we do wrong as if forced. Krishna names desire, which turns into anger, as the enemy that clouds wisdom like smoke over fire, and tells him to master it.
prasang.lesson: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.

why: 'why do I do the wrong thing even when I do not want to', asked without excuse
Why do I keep doing the thing I don't want to do, as if something pushes me?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks what drives people to do wrong against their will; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचकाम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः । महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥
verse.line: It's desire, which turns into anger when blocked. Never satisfied, it is the real enemy here.
verse.translation: The Blessed Lord said: It is desire, it is anger, born of the quality of passion; all-devouring and greatly harmful. Know this to be the enemy here.

words.en: born from the quality of passion

verse.why: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.

prasang.title: Restraining desire
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks why we do wrong as if forced. Krishna names desire, which turns into anger, as the enemy that clouds wisdom like smoke over fire, and tells him to master it.
prasang.lesson: Desire unmet becomes anger; see it clearly and you can master it.

why: what drove the act is named as an enemy to be known, not as who you are

guard.line: Every living being is an eternal part of me, says Krishna.

verse.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verse.setting: The refrain closing each of Uddalaka's lessons.
verse.sanskrit: स य एषोऽणिमैतदात्म्यमिदꣳ सर्वं तत्सत्यꣳ स आत्मा तत्त्वमसि श्वेतकेतो इति भूय एव मा भगवान्विज्ञापयत्विति तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
verse.line: That subtle essence is the self of all that is. That is truth. You are that, Shvetaketu.
verse.translation: That which is the subtle essence: this whole world has it as its self. That is the truth. That is the self. That you are, Shvetaketu. 'Teach me more, sir.' 'So be it, dear one.'
verse.why: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.

prasang.title: Uddalaka's lessons: tat tvam asi
prasang.summary: Uddalaka teaches his son through everyday experiments: a fast that dims the mind, a bird on a string, rivers merging in the sea, a banyan seed with nothing visible inside, salt dissolved in water, a blindfolded man finding his way home. Each lesson ends: 'That subtle essence is the self of all. You are that, Shvetaketu.'
prasang.lesson: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.

why: the self the verse points to is not the one that failed
What you are is not small.

verse.speaker: Teacher
verse.setting: A catechism of definitions: 'What is caste?'
verse.sanskrit: जातिरिति च न चर्मणो न रक्तस्य न मांसस्य न चास्थिनः । न जातिरात्मनो जातिर्व्यवहारप्रकल्पिता ।
verse.line: Caste is not in skin, blood, flesh or bone. The self has no caste; caste is a social convention.
verse.translation: And what is caste? It is not of the skin, nor of the blood, nor of the flesh, nor of the bones. The self has no caste; caste is a convention made for worldly dealings.

why: shame about origin has nothing in the self to attach to
a label fixed at birth is denied any hold on what one is

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.setting: 'My Plan of Campaign', Victoria Hall, Madras, February 1897.
verse.line: anything that makes you weak physically, intellectually, and spiritually, reject as poison;
verse.translation: And here is the test of truth — anything that makes you weak physically, intellectually, and spiritually, reject as poison; there is no life in it, it cannot be true. Truth is strengthening.
verse.why: Judge ideas, and habits, by whether they make you stronger.

prasang.title: 'Reject it as poison' (Madras, 1897)
prasang.summary: He answers critics who claimed others made his American success, noting how quickly sympathy vanishes when you dare to differ. His test of truth: whatever makes you weak in body, mind or spirit, reject as poison.
prasang.lesson: Judge ideas, and habits, by whether they make you stronger.

why: choose what strengthens

verse.speaker: Shiva
verse.setting: Shiva, when Sati wants to attend her father's ceremony uninvited, where Shiva is resented.
verse.sanskrit: जदपि मित्र प्रभु पितु गुर गेहा। जाइअ बिनु बोलेहुँ न सँदेहा॥ तदपि बिरोध मान जहँ कोई। तहाँ गएँ कल्यानु न होई ॥
verse.line: You may visit family without an invitation. But where there is hostility toward you, going brings no good.
verse.translation: It is true that one may go uninvited to the home of a friend, a master, a father or a teacher. Yet where someone holds hostility toward you, no good comes of going there.
verse.why: You may go to family without an invitation, but not into open hostility; listen to that warning.
verse.misuse: Not a rule to cut off family; a caution about walking into known hostility.

prasang.title: Sati goes to her father's sacrifice uninvited
prasang.summary: Sati's father Daksha holds a great sacrifice and invites everyone except Shiva and her. Shiva warns her that going where there is hostility brings no good, but she goes. Her father ignores her and insults her husband in front of everyone, and the visit ends in catastrophe.
prasang.story_hook: The sky over Kailash filled with chariots heading to her father's feast, and none of them had come for her.
prasang.lesson: You may go to family without an invitation, but not into open hostility; listen to that warning.

why: self-respect may decline a room that holds contempt

story.title: Vairagyashatakam: Censure of craving
story.summary: The poet confesses everything he did for money and approval: digging for treasure, flattering kings, forcing laughter. He ends with the famous lines that pleasures consumed us and craving never aged, and hope pictured as a river.
story.lesson: We think we are chasing things; really, the chase is using up our lives.

plan_v3.path: st.bh.forced_laughter_before_fools -enacts_in-> dainya, glani ; st.bh.forced_laughter_before_fools -enacts_turn-> tejas ; st.bh.forced_laughter_before_fools -fits_situation-> self_worth
why: It is our own hope of gain that makes us flatter and smile on cue; seeing that is the start of dignity.
